data.raw_text:
Cuba just went from rhetoric to secondary sanctions to 60% of its shipping halted. I flagged that front 50 days ago as one of six. Here's what aged, what didn't, and what I missed.

On March 28, I posted that every adversary was accelerating while the US burned $1-2B/day in the Gulf. Six fronts: Taiwan, THAAD/Korea, North Korea, Russia, China trade, Cuba. 50 days later the picture is sharper than the original thesis, and uneven enough to be worth auditing in public.

AGED BEST: CUBA

Trump said "Cuba's next" the day before that post. I flagged it as speculative. It is now operational policy.
- May 1: Trump EO expanding secondary sanctions to non-US firms in key Cuban sectors. Largest move against non-US entities in decades.
- May 17: CMA CGM and Hapag-Lloyd suspended Cuba bookings. ~60% of Cuba shipping volume at risk.
- Diesel shortages, severe blackouts, Havana protests.
- DOJ preparing criminal charges against Raúl Castro this week.
- Today: Kobeissi reports 300 drones, Russian and Iranian supply chain since 2023, CIA Director Ratcliffe personally warning Havana.

Full-spectrum economic siege with a security pretext quietly being assembled.

AGED PARTIAL: NORTH KOREA

12 missile launches in a month was the original flag. The real story is the production stack underneath.
- IAEA warned of "very serious" expansion in NK nuclear weapons production. Probable new enrichment facility at Yongbyon.
- Pyongyang declared it is not bound by NPT obligations.
- ~14,000 NK troops fighting for Russia. Western estimates put NK deaths above 6,000.
- NK accumulating battlefield experience and tech transfer from a live European war while expanding warhead output.

Not a launch-count story. Missiles + warheads + industrial base + war integration with Moscow.

AGED PARTIAL: RUSSIA / UKRAINE

Spring offensive happened. Character shifted.
- Gerasimov claimed 1,700 sq km taken in 2026. Ukrainian-aligned maps say ~600.
- Fighting at outskirts of Kostiantynivka. Pokrovsk and Sumy under pressure.
- May 14: heaviest two-day aerial assault of the entire war. 1,567 drones, 56 missiles. 27 civilians killed.

Right on direction. The escalation is in the skies faster than on the ground.

AGED PARTIAL: TAIWAN

Real escalation, but coercive shaping, not invasion conditions.
- Near-daily PLA air and naval activity.
- Xi told Trump mishandling Taiwan could send relations to a "dangerous place."
- Taiwan only passed two-thirds of Lai's $40B special defense budget.
- Possible second $14B US arms package still unclear.

Gray-zone pressure, not pre-assault mobilization.

AGED PARTIAL: CHINA TRADE

The legal scaffolding I flagged is in place. The active coercion is operating elsewhere.
- Heavy rare-earth exports (yttrium, dysprosium, terbium) ~50% below pre-control levels. Yttrium prices outside China up roughly 140x.
- Selective licensing, MATCH Act counter-decrees, direct industry lobbying.
- Xi-Trump summit produced stabilization, not resolution. $17B/year ag commitment is less than half phase-one.

Beijing has room to squeeze again without formally ending the truce.

GOT WRONG: THAAD

This is the one to log openly.

I wrote the US moved THAAD from Korea to the Gulf. The accurate fact pattern:
- Patriots and munitions were diverted forward to support the Iran war.
- Patriot launchers were photographed at Osan.
- But on April 21, USFK commander Gen. Brunson told the Senate that no THAAD systems were moved from South Korea.

Asian deterrence was stressed, not stripped. The allocation pressure point stands. The specific THAAD claim was wrong. Logging it.

MISSED: SOUTH CHINA SEA

China tightened control at Scarborough Shoal entrance. Live-fire drills near Luzon during Balikatan. Personnel placed on Sandy Cay with a Chinese flag. Manila publicly downplayed reduced US deterrence but warned Beijing could exploit any opening.

Exactly the kind of gray-zone theater that gets bolder when Washington is tied up elsewhere.

MISSED: US AND ALLIED MISSILE STOCKPILE STRAIN

This is the most important variable I missed in March. It is the mechanism that connects every other front.
- Iran war cost the US $29-60+B as of May 12.
- Washington warned European allies of weapons-delivery delays from war-driven stockpile drain.
- Switzerland told Patriot deliveries could be delayed 5 to 7 years.
- Korea Patriot redeployment discussions and visible asset shuffling.

This is how a Gulf war weakens deterrence everywhere. Not by emptying Asia. By forcing painful allocation choices across multiple theaters at once.

THE STRUCTURAL READ

The original thesis was "every front accelerates simultaneously." The accurate version, 50 days later: every front is under pressure, unevenly, and the deeper risk is that US interceptors, munitions, and diplomatic bandwidth are stretched across too many theaters at once.

This maps directly to the plumbing thread I posted earlier today. G7 long-end yields at 22-year highs. JGB 30Y at 4% for the first time. Japan dumping US Treasuries at the fastest pace in four years. The plumbing IS the fiscal language of the same constraint.

One overstretched issuer trying to fund: Gulf war, European allies, Asian deterrence, Caribbean coercion campaign, and AI capex commitments. Geopolitical bandwidth and fiscal bandwidth are the same constraint expressed in two languages.

The trade is positioning for that constraint to bind in stages. Stage 1, current: long-end yields rip, energy substitution accelerates, single-name vol spikes. Stage 2: credit. Stage 3: index catches up.

Reflation thesis intact. Bonds and USD remain the underweights.

Two languages. One constraint.
